ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, there are two carts on a long straight horizontal track. Cart A is moving to the left with a speed of $v_{1}$, and Cart B is moving to the right with a speed of $v_{2}$. Cart A is equipped with a gun that fires a bullet horizontally every $\Delta t_{0}$ time interval, and each bullet hits the target mounted on Cart B. Ignoring the gravity and air resistance of the bullets, the speed of each bullet relative to the ground remains constant at $v_{0}$. Each bullet hits the target when the next bullet has already been fired. Assume that the speeds of the two carts are not affected by the firing of the bullets.

1. The distance between two adjacent bullets in the air is $s$.
2. The time interval $\Delta t$ between two consecutive bullets hitting the target

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal straight track, with two small cars on it. The small car on the left is labeled A, and on the car is mounted a gun horizontally pointing to the right; the velocity arrow v_1 beside A points to the left. The small car on the right is labeled B, and on the car there is a target; the velocity arrow v_2 beside B points to the right. Between the muzzle and the target are drawn a horizontal dashed line and a bullet, and the bullet velocity is labeled v_0, with direction to the right. Reasoning: Take the ground reference frame, and establish the x axis with rightward as positive. Let the time of the first firing be t=0, the muzzle position x=0, and the initial position of the target x=D. Car A moves leftward with velocity v_1, so the nth bullet is fired at t=n\Delta t_0 from the position x=-v_1 n\Delta t_0. The velocity of the bullet relative to the ground remains v_0, with direction to the right, therefore the trajectory of the nth bullet after firing is x_n(t)=-v_1 n\Delta t_0+v_0(t-n\Delta t_0)=v_0t-(v_0+v_1)n\Delta t_0. 1. At any common time t, when the nth and the n+1th bullets are both already in the air, their position difference is x_n(t)-x_{n+1}(t)=[v_0t-(v_0+v_1)n\Delta t_0]-[v_0t-(v_0+v_1)(n+1)\Delta t_0]=(v_0+v_1)\Delta t_0. Therefore the distance between two adjacent bullets in the air is s=(v_0+v_1)\Delta t_0. 2. The position of the target on car B is x_B(t)=D+v_2t. When the nth bullet hits the target, it satisfies v_0t-(v_0+v_1)n\Delta t_0=D+v_2t, so t_n=\frac{D+(v_0+v_1)n\Delta t_0}{v_0-v_2}. The time interval for two consecutive bullets to hit the target is \Delta t=t_{n+1}-t_n=\frac{(v_0+v_1)\Delta t_0}{v_0-v_2}.
